stories.title: Riyadh airport: 12 dead, 309 hurt; Trump weighs joining Saudi strikes on Houthis
facts: Material update: Saudi GACA says ≥12 killed and ~309 injured at King Khalid Airport — four Saudis, two Bangladeshis, plus one each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt (Al Jazeera / Reuters).
Deadliest attack in the kingdom in more than a decade; third Houthi hit on Riyadh’s airport this week. Flights to/from Riyadh remain suspended or diverted (ABC / Australian travel advice).
Trump called the attack “terrible,” said he will speak with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and that the US is evaluating whether to join Saudi strikes on the Houthis — “We’ll move very quickly.”

SecState Rubio: an American was among the dead. UN Sec-Gen Guterres and envoy Hans Grundberg condemned attacks on civilian airports as a grave escalation; Egypt, Qatar, Pakistan, Jordan, Canada and others also condemned.
Germany’s Auswärtiges Amt already warned against using Riyadh airport Saturday evening; Australia now says do not travel to King Khalid International.
stories.whyItMatters: A confirmed mass-casualty toll plus an open US debate on striking the Houthis turns Saturday’s airport hit into a wider Gulf escalation risk for travelers and energy routes.

stories.title: US disables tanker running Iran blockade; IRGC claims Hormuz strike
facts: CENTCOM: US jet struck the stern of Panama-flagged M/V Ocean Molica (aka Arika Sun) in the Gulf of Oman Sat after it ignored warnings and tried to run the Iran-port blockade — propulsion out, crew unharmed.
CENTCOM says the blockade (resumed 14 Jul) has disabled four commercial vessels and turned around 135 ships in three months, and destroyed 10 IRGC-linked shadow-fleet tankers.
IRGC claims it struck LPG carrier NV Sunshine (NatWit) for taking an “illegal” southern Hormuz route; UKMTO separately reported an outbound tanker hit on the port side with a fire, crew safe.
Sen. Chris Murphy criticized the US strike as taxpayers “paying billions to hit commercial ships.” About a fifth of world oil/LNG used to transit Hormuz before the war.
stories.whyItMatters: Parallel US and Iranian enforcement of rival Gulf blockades keeps tanker risk elevated even when the Riyadh story dominates the headlines.

stories.title: DOJ probes ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC and Fox over Trump pool coverage pause
facts: Justice Department Antitrust Division is investigating whether major TV networks violated the Sherman Act when they briefly suspended White House pool coverage last month (BBC / NYT).

Targets named in coverage: ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC and Fox News — DOJ asked for pool-related communications after the networks paused coverage when the administration pulled credentials for CNN, MS Now and Politico.
Those three outlets later regained access after suing; a judge restored credentials. Networks have not commented on the probe.
Context: White House took control of the press pool from the Correspondents’ Association earlier in 2026; separate fights continue over AP access and “Gulf of America” naming.
stories.whyItMatters: Treating a collective press-pool protest as a potential antitrust boycott is a new pressure tool against US broadcast news.

stories.title: Isaias aftermath: at least 4 dead; ~438k still without power Sat night
facts: Material update: ABC confirms ≥4 storm deaths — two in Escambia Co., Fla. (tree into home; generator in garage) and two in Alabama (incl. Jefferson Co. tree-on-house).
Sat night: >438k customers without power across FL/AL/GA (≈345k Fla., ≈82k Ala., >10k Ga.) after Cat-2 landfall near Destin Fri ~20:30 CT / 105 mph.
DeSantis: statewide accounts without power were ~439k as of Sat 1 p.m.; FPL said it restored >43k by late morning Sat with a ~16k-person restoration workforce.
Remnants bring level-3 flash-flood risk into NE Georgia / western Carolinas (Athens, Greenville, Asheville corridor); Destin–Fort Walton / Pensacola airports still closed into Saturday.
stories.whyItMatters: The death toll and multi-day outage map matter more than the landfall itself now that the storm is post-tropical.
